text_blocks.snippet: Cushing's syndrome diagnosis involves confirming hypercortisolism through biochemical tests and then determining the cause. Initial screening tests include measuring urine cortisol, late-night salivary cortisol, or using the 1-mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test. Further tests, like ACTH measurement and imaging scans, help pinpoint the source of the excess cortisol.
